## ## **Runesmithing**
Runesmiths and Runic magic 

The Dwarfs count no wizards, nor spellcasters of any sort, among their number. This, the Dwarfs affirm, is not by accident or lack of ability, but rather the benefit of good common sense and a natural resistance to all things magical. Dwarfs believe magic to be a wild and fickle thing, corrupting by its very nature, and safe only when hammered into obedience. Those capable of just such a feat are known as Runesmiths. 

Legends are told among the Dwarfs of how the ancestor god Thungni, son of Grungni and Valaya, handed down the knowledge of rune crafting to his seven apprentices, and how they carried the knowledge to each of the great Dwarf holds. Generations later, those same runes are still crafted by their descendants, a sacredlink back to their creator. The runes hold a mystical place in Dwarf culture, and many Dwarfs dream of owning a weapon or item engraved with a rune. Across the Old World and beyond, Dwarfs are known as master craftsmen of magical items and their secrets are jealousy guarded. 

Rune crafting, sometimes called Runic Magic, much to the annoyance of Runesmiths, is a highly disciplined craft. Every Runesmith worth of the name is a talented and highly trained Dwarf, capable of binding aspects of the winds of magic to runes inscribed on and formed of metal or stone. Like the Dwarfs themselves, runes are a reliable and sturdy means of wielding magic, though this approach does mean there are limits to how it can be used, as there are limits as to how much power can be contained. 

It is a very powerful craft that takes a long time to master and a long time to perform, resulting in runes that were handed to the Dwarfs from the Ancestor Gods themselves. 

Runesmiths do not share the knowledge of their craft even between other Dwarfs, with the only exception being their apprentices of the craft. They share the secrets of runecraft by word of mouth alone. 

## **Apprentices**
Runesmiths are duty-bound to seek out apprentices to enable them to pass on knowledge of the runes. Some Runesmith craft guilds only admit those who can trace their clan ancestry back to Thungni’s apprentices, though some break with tradition and, controversially, simply seek those with the right mix of talent and dedication. Such practices have become more common in recent decades, with some Runesmiths grumbling that the old ways are precisely why there are so few apprentices, and why so much knowledge has been lost. 

On taking an apprentice, the master arranges for the leather apron of an apprentice to be made. This is presented to the apprentice during their formal initiation, where they swear their oaths. Apprentices learn how to craft by working with their masters or others in the craft guild, assisting in their work or undertaking menial tasks. By rights, a master may demand that even a high apprentice undertake such tasks. Most Runesmiths are far too clever to seek to make enemies of their colleagues, however, and leave such work to the beardlings. 

## **A Secret Knowledge**
Dwarf runesmithing is a waning practice. As more Dwarfs die without passing on their knowledge, said knowledge is being lost to the next generations. Therefore Dwarf runesmithing and runic artefacts are incredibly valued among Dwarfs. 

## **Runesmiths**
Those who successfully pass the life of an apprentice are initiated into the Guild of Runesmiths, one of the oldest of the craft guilds. Being a Runesmith means a life of near-endless study, with each level of mastery bringing fresh insight as to just how many ancient secrets and hidden techniques there are still to learn. 

XI **I** X **VI** XI **I** 

All influential craft guilds are subject to often bitter disagreements, and the Guild of Runesmiths is no different. Arguments between different Runesmith clans, and with other guilds, is common. There is often also heated debate on whether or not a particular candidate would make a suitable apprentice and, more rarely and more bitterly, whether a particular Runesmith would make an acceptable master. These disagreements and feuds are another contributing factor to the slow loss of knowledge that afflicts the Guild, but, like many Dwarfs, most Runesmiths are stubborn, and so this obvious and existential threat goes unremedied. 

There are strict laws about the creation and possession of runic items, although they can differ from hold to hold. Items inscribed with permanent runes may not be sold to or created for any Dwarf without a Runelord’s permission. Creating an item for a non-Dwarf must also have the authority of the leader of the hold. 

This information on the owner of an item is recorded in the records of the guild, and some guilds record the deeds of the item. Many holds retain notional ownership of all items created there, deeding them to the owner for a certain number of years or, occasionally, generations. This has led to friction with certain noble houses, who were angered to find a Dwarf emissary on their door demanding the return of what, to them, was a hallowed family heirloom. 

Items with temporary runes have less restriction. Although Runesmiths are charged to create even these lesser items only for proven friends of the Dwarfs, the definition of ‘friend’ is sometimes interpreted quite widely, particularly in the Empire. 

Runic items are treated with care and reverence. Most are prized possessions, precious heirlooms or ceremonial items owned in common by an entire hold. To be chosen as the bearer of such an item is a great honour — Dwarfs who have disgraced such an office are expected to take the Slayer’s Oath. 

## **The Heart of the Hold**
Located at the centre of most Dwarf holds is the Anvil Forge, home to an endless chorus of hammer strikes, the roar of furnaces, and the skillful inscribing of runes. Most Anvil Forges consist of a single great forge, several smaller smelters and foundries, racks of tools, and countless other paraphernalia associated with smithing, all neatly arranged. If a hold is lucky enough to possess an Anvil of Doom, one of the great anvils forged in ancient times and bedecked in runes no living Runesmith could hope to duplicate, it will be stored here. 

An Anvil of Doom is used to strike the master runes that would shatter any lesser anvil, and are always treated with great reverence and care. Occasionally, they are removed and brought to battle, the better to empower a mighty Runelord and bring death and ruination to the hold’s foes. 

Runesmiths see the anvil as representing the mind of the hold, and the forge its heart. This is not a view that everyone agrees with, particularly the other craft guilds who, though they may hold their tongue in public, sometimes see Runesmiths as an arrogant and self-aggrandising lot. This tension occasionally turns to barroom violence between rival apprentices. Recently, a senior jewel smith grandmaster at Karak Azul was chastised for encouraging attacks on Runesmith apprentices in response to an insult he had received. 

XI **I** X **VI** XI **I** 

Radiating from the forge room are workrooms, smaller forges, storerooms, living quarters and mines. The most senior Runesmiths have their own workshops. The entrances are guarded by Dwarfs sworn to the guild, and only members and escorted guests are allowed to enter. Some holds allow the rulers of the hold to enter unescorted, but not all, and this is usually an indication of a tense relationship. Guards are also permitted to search visitors as they leave, although this is rarely done, especially with other Dwarfs. 

During working hours, and the guilds work long hours, the central area around the forge room bustles with the sound of crafting and litanies echoing through the tunnels. The main forge is kept burning throughout the year except for the two days before Zagazdeg when it is allowed to cool before being ceremonially relit on the day of the festival. On this day, an open invitation is given to all those in the hold to join the Runesmiths in celebration. 

Hidden away from casual visitors, some Runesmith craft guilds maintain a wall of grudges, eschewing paper for stone, the original material upon which runes were struck. Many walls were lost when the Karak’s fell, much to the pain of the guilds. Karak Hirn has a floor of grudges, and those walking across are invited to remind themselves each time of every outstanding grudge they step across. Whether floor or wall, a mark is put next to any completed grudges to show its completion. 

## **A Seal Unbroken**
unknown to outsiders, and even to most Runesmiths who do not hold the title of Runelord, forges used for runesmithing must sometimes be dismantled, their every stone sealed away deep beneath the craft guild. this occurs when a forge becomes corrupted by the touch of chaos — a rare event, and one which seems to trouble only the oldest forges. some suspect this is because the practice of runesmithing imposes order on chaotic magic, and the essence of corruption this expels slowly builds up over millennia, often leading to strange occurrences.

## **Anvils of Doom**
The greatest items of Dwarf legend were created upon an Anvil of Doom, unique artefacts of ancient times, each of which contains immense magical power. These large anvils are said to have been created by the Runelord Kurgaz and his descendants, under Thunder Mountain, using the energy of the volcano’s heart to forge the rare metal gromnil into shape. Each Anvil was inscribed with numerous runes, many of which are long forgotten. 

The Anvils were spread amongst the holds and given to the Runesmith craft guilds to guard, although many now say that their craft guild owns them. Individuals claim a rare few. A number of anvils were lost when the Karaks fell and are a source of great shame for those craft guilds who greatly desire their return. 

Some anvils are also dedicated (jointly along with Thungni) to an ancestor god, and these represent the focus of the clan. Those dedicated to Grimnir emphasise a focus on battle, those dedicated to Grungni emphasise effort and protection, while those dedicated to Valaya emphasise learning and the home. 

Those craft guilds that claim ownership (temporarily or not) of an anvil strictly control access to them. Outsiders to the clan must petition the senior members of the clan. Access is rarely refused outright, but the times are restricted or not given for months or years. While some of this reflects the use of a limited resource, the clan allocate based on relationship to the clan, the honour it will bring, the need for the item, or hold politics; with Dwarfs of the Empire always feeling like the poor cousins. 

Rarely, an Anvil of Doom will be brought to the battlefield, always attended by a trusted Runelord. They can provide a point of central defence if the hold has been breached or, occasionally, they are taken to battlefields further afield. Anvils of Doom are rare and precious items and their loss would be sorely felt by the Runesmiths, so their presence on the battlefield is a matter of last resort. The anvil of Karak Drazh was lost at the battle of Red Water shortly before the hold fell, and its use on that day is now a byword for foolishness. Rumours circulate that this relic is now in the hands of Imperial Dwarfs living in the Empire, hidden because of their frustration at the lack of easy access to other anvils. 

You practice the magical runecraft of your people, infusing a physical object with arcane power. the full rules for crafting runes can be found on page 125.

## **Runesmiths in Campaigns**
Rune items are powerful additions to a game and Gamesmasters will consider carefully how they are included. Finding a rune weapon can involve unwanted attention from Dwarfs, especially the Order of Hrungil, who hunt down wayward runic items and rogue Runesmiths. A runic weapon is a prize almost anyone might attempt to claim, however, so those openly bearing them must be wary of those showing undue interest in these vaunted relics. 

Few Characters would turn down the opportunity to gain a runic item, but how they interact with Runesmiths will depend to a large degree on whether they are Dwarf. Most Runesmiths will deal only with other Dwarfs or those who are formally introduced to them by a Dwarf in good standing. However, Runesmiths are secretive by nature, and even this is no guarantee of a warm reception. Simply asking a Runesmith to create an item is unlikely to work, and the process of gaining their cooperation is rarely straightforward. Runesmiths see their craft as a blessing from the Ancestor Gods, and so coin alone will not suffice as payment. Characters may be asked to do some service for the Dwarf or their hold and will need to prove why they are worthy to carry such an item. 

The purchase of temporary runes is not as onerous, but the Runesmith will still want to be satisfied as to the Character’s intent. Those asking a Runesmith about a runic item they have discovered will find themselves answering a lot of questions before they get a response. 

Runesmiths do sometimes require the help of adventurous sorts. Runelords need ingredients to create or inscribe master runes, especially if they see to create a new — a ruinously expensive process undertaken over years by only the most experienced Runelords. Some prefer to use individuals from outside their hold so as not to give away any secrets to their rivals. Others are in search of more ancient material that they are not supposed to be seeking, and will pay outsiders well for service and discretion. 

Dwarf Characters who wish to become a Runesmith will need to convince one to become their master. The Runesmith may require them to undertake some trials to prove their worth. On passing their apprenticeship, some Runesmiths are sent into the wider world in service of their craft guild, obtaining knowledge or searching for lost runes and ingredients. 

Characters may also find themselves in the middle of the politics and tension that exist between Imperial Dwarfs and those living in the Empire or even between Dwarfs in different holds. They could be asked to act as spies to discover Runesmiths making and selling runes illegally by either Dwarf or authorities in the Empire. 

## **Runesmiths in the Empire**
The Empire has no official view of Dwarf Runesmiths. Many magisters and Witch hunters have tried to make the case that it is an unlicensed magical art and should be outlawed. Few have enough experience of the practice to recognise that it is less dangerous than most magical practices, and would likely not care even if they did. however, most of the empire’s ruling class recognise that it would be politically ruinous to challenge this ancient Dwarf custom, especially when so many of the Empire’s own symbols of office and magical weapons  — the vaunted Runefangs of the elector Counts among them — are the product of this craft. nevertheless, most Runesmiths in the empire think it sensible to keep a low profile, though they have another reason for doing so. 

Anyone can recognise the power of the runes, and humans in the empire and elsewhere have ever been drawn to power. some even claim to have mastered the secrets of Dwarf Runes themselves. this is little more than base charlatanry, the crass efforts of unscrupulous manlings to grift a handful of shillings from unsuspecting buyers. however, just as with attempts to pass off human craft as superior Dwarf handiwork, the Dwarfs themselves take this very seriously indeed. While the emperor views such crimes as civil matters, to be handled with fines or perhaps an afternoon in the stocks, to a Dwarf the matter is far more grave. 

A ring of such forgers and charlatans currently operates out of Kemperbad, passing off rough ales spiked with spirits as true Dwarfen brew, passable tools as the product of Dwarf craftsmanship, and perhaps most grievously, several impressive if gaudy arms as Dwarf runic weapons of various sorts. though several Dwarf holds, as well as local imperial Dwarf merchants, have complained, Kemperbad’s Council has failed to take the matter seriously enough. Any Dwarf who took care of these unscrupulous traders in a more appropriate way would likely win a good deal of thanks. moreover, if the matter is not resolved soon, it is likely to escalate ruinously, threatening Dwarf-human relations in the region.

## Crafting Runes
Crafting a permanent magic rune requires a great deal of work and time — often days, weeks, or even years. Characters rarely have the opportunity to undertake labour of this magnitude in the field, and will more commonly work their trade by using the _Forge Rune_ Endeavour between adventures. 

To forge a rune, choose one of the runes or master runes you have learned through Talents. Runes are always forged onto an existing, physical item, so you need to already own, purchase, or steal the Trapping you’re inscribing the rune onto. Runesmithing also requires you to have your own Trade Tools (Smith), and access to a Workshop. If you don’t have your own Workshop, you can work in your mentor’s forge, or request access to a peer’s Workshop as a Minor Favour ( **WFRP Core Rulebook** ). The actual forging process is resolved as an Extended Test. You can make one Test per week or Endeavour — a **Challenging (+0) Runesmithing** Test if forging a rune, or a **Hard (-20) Runesmithing** Test if forging a master rune. The number of SLs required to complete the process is specified in the rune’s description. 

## **The Silent Sibling**
When thungni handed down the secrets of the runes to his apprentices, they left to form the original Runesmith Clans and craft guilds. One apprentice was lost to history, and some speculate that this is because of a deliberate effort some time in the past to obscure their fate. the lost apprentice became known as the silent sibling, although it is not clear why. Rumours of this Runesmith run through the centuries, telling of secret knowledge, forbidden cults, or a refined and more powerful form of Runesmithing. 

the silent sibling is often evoked by those who want to lend legitimacy to actions outside of mainstream Dwarf culture. groups of failed apprentices, believing themselves deprived of their birthright by haughty Runelords, sometimes meet in secret. these groups style themselves as apprenticed to the silent sibling, and put to use what little they do know in crafting runes and items of uncertain power. they are ever in search of more knowledge about their craft, though any Runemaster in good standing would know enough to keep well enough away from such desperate Dwarfs. 

If the Extended Test is successful, the rune is successfully inscribed upon the target Trapping, transforming it into a runic item. Runic weapons, armour, etc. all count as magical items. 

## **Rules of the Runes**
There are many restrictions on which magical runes can be applied to which surfaces, learned by a Runesmith as part of their apprenticeship. The rules below are those most commonly relevant. 

## **Rule of Three**
No runic item can be inscribed with more than three runes. Unless the crafter is possessed of a once-in-ageneration talent, all Tests to inscribe a fourth rune onto an item automatically fail. 

A runic item may be inscribed with duplicates of the same rune, unless it is a master rune (see the Rule of Jealousy). The runes listed below explain the effects of a duplicated rune upon a runic item. Note that the effects of duplicate runes on the same runic item stack, but effects of duplicate runes on different runic items do not — creatures are only affected by whichever runic item has the most versions of that rune. 

XI **I** X **VI** XI **I** 

## **Rule of Form**
Each of the categories of rune have specific rules about what items they can be forged upon. This is mostly selfexplanatory —a weapon rune cannot be forged upon a crown, and so on. 

Furthermore, runes can only be applied to materials suitable for permanent inscription, typically metal, stone, or jewels. Runes cannot be traced in sand, or marked with chalk, or painted on a wall. Runes cannot be forged on magical items, except those already marked with a Dwarfen rune magic. It is very rare for a rune to be forged upon an object not crafted by Dwarfen hands. 

Runesmiths seldom experiment with new uses for their craft, but if a Character wants to bend the Rule of Form slightly — e.g. affixing a weapon rune to a spear, a talismanic rune to a cloak, or an engineering rune to a flame cannon — the GM may allow them to proceed with a negative modifier on their Runesmithing Tests. 

## **Rule of Jealousy**
A runic item may not be inscribed with more than one master rune. If more than one version of the same master rune appears within 100 yards of each other, then only the oldest master rune continues to function. All other iterations of that master rune are rendered inert, as described in the Rule of Pride. 

## **Flawed Creations**
A proud Dwarf Runesmith would never intentionally forge a rune that had suboptimal or intermittent effects. However, mistakes can happen, and it is not uncommon for a rune to appear functional, but reveal its shortcomings in the heat of battle. 

When you conclude a _Forge Rune_ Endeavour, you may choose to introduce a Runic Flaw to the rune you’re crafting. This provides an immediate +5 SL towards the ongoing Extended Test. A rune can only have one Runic Flaw, and in most instances, it is only worth acquiring one if the rune is needed in time for the next adventure. 

## **Rule of Pride**
Outside of their apprenticeship, Runesmiths do not like to repeat their work, or imitate the works of others. If a runic item is within 100 yards of another runic item bearing the same combination of runes — including items that both bear the same single rune — then only the oldest runic item continues to function. All other imitators are rendered inert, deactivating their runes until the duplicate runic item is at least 100 yards away. 

A Runic Flaw is slow to materialise, and the Runesmith may not realise they have made a mistake. However, the first time a completed rune with a Runic Flaw activates its effects during an adventure, roll 1d10 and consult the Runic Flaw table to determine its effects. 

Very rarely, a pair or small collection of runic items created together might be exempt from this rule. The twelve Runefangs gifted to the Empire are the best known exception. 

## **Runic Flaws Table**
| 1d10 | Runic Flaw |
|---|---|
| 1 | The rune functions as intended for the next minute… after which, the runic item is consumed by its improperly contained power, destroying the Trapping and all runes it currently bears. |
| 2-3 | The rune functions as intended for the next minute, before its power is exhausted and dispersed into the Winds of Mag yed, and must be forged from scratch. ic. The rune is destro |
| 4-5 | The rune functions as intended for the rest of the adventure, before it fades and loses its power, and must be forged from scratch. |
| 6-8 | The rune inflicts 1 point of Damage upon the Trapping it’s inscribed upon. It inflicts 1 additional point of Damage upon the runic item at the start of each adventure. |
| 9-10 | The rune is sluggish to activate — whenever the bearer wishes to use its effects, they must spend 1 Fortune point to do so. |

## List of Runes
A Character can learn any of the runes in this list using the Runic Magic or Master Rune Magic (page 80) Talents. 

## **Weapon Runes**
Weapon runes can only be forged upon a melee weapon — an axe, a hammer, or very occasionally a sword. They cannot be crafted onto an Engineering weapon or a ranged weapon. 

## **Rune of Cleaving**
## **Sls Required** : 10
The weapon inflicts +1 Damage for each Rune of Cleaving. 

For purposes of activating _Dual Wielder_ , you may count a weapon bearing the Rune of Fury as two separate weapons, one in each hand, allowing you to attack two targets even if you aren’t carrying a second weapon. 

## **Grudge Rune**
## **Sls Required** : 10
Nominate an enemy you bear a Blood Grudge (page 84). For each Grudge Rune, the weapon gains both +10 to hit and +1 Damage on attacks against the target. At the end of the adventure, if your nominated enemy is slain, you may nominate a new target against whom you bear a Blood Grudge.

## **Rune of Fire**
## **Sls Required** : 16
Once drawn, the weapon’s blade bursts into flames, providing 20 yards of illumination, and inflicting 1 _Ablaze_ Condition on enemies it inflicts damage upon. This attack deals no Damage, but inflicts 1 _Ablaze_ Condition for each Rune of Fire. 

When attacking with this weapon, you gain +10 to your Melee Skill for each Rune of Striking (the specialisation for the Melee Skill being the same as the Weapon Type of the weapon upon which the rune is inscribed). 

Note that the bonus only applies to strikes with this weapon, so if you are dual wielding with a similar weapon, attacks made with that weapon do not benefit from the bonus.

## **Master Rune of Steel**
## **Sls Required** : 20
Whilst wearing this armour, you can only suffer a maximum of 10 Wounds from any instance when Damage is inflicted. 

## **Runic Talismans**
Runic Talismans can only be forged upon jewellery or other personal effects — most commonly rings, for convenience, but also amulets, jewels, belts, crowns, robes, warhorns or, where appropriate, a drinking vessel. 

## **Rune of Clear Sight**
## **Sls Required** : 8
When the talisman is pressed to your eye, you negate any penalties imposed by fog, mist, smoke, or other clouding, non-magical vapours. Two Runes of Clear Seeing also penetrate magical vapours. Two Runes of Clear Seeing allow you to see clearly even in total darkness. 

## **Rune of  Truth**
## **Sls Required** : 8
The talisman glows brightly if pressed into contact with an item that has been faked, forged, counterfeited, or deliberately degraded in value. Two Runes of Disclosure also identify magical illusions or duplicates. Three Runes of Disclosure reveal the precise method of deception to the bearer. 

## **Rune of Restoration**
## **Sls Required** : 10
After a good night’s sleep whilst wearing this talisman, the bearer regains their Toughness Bonus in Wounds for each Rune of Restoration. 

## **Rune of Spellbreaking**
## **Sls Required** : 10
Whilst wearing this talisman, and using the _Magic Resistance_ Talent, you can activate a Rune of Spellbreaking to automatically count as rolling 01 on your Willpower Test. You can activate each Rune of Spellbreaking once per adventure, and must choose to activate it before you roll. 

## **Rune of Spelleating**
## **Sls Required** : 10
If you successfully dispel a spell using the _Magic Resistance_ Talent whilst wearing this talisman, the spellcaster cannot attempt the spell again for your Willpower Bonus in Rounds. Two Runes of Spelleating extend this effect to your Willpower Bonus in hours. Three Runes of Spelleating extend this effect to your Willpower Bonus in weeks.

## **Sls Required** : 15
Whilst wearing this talisman, you may impose a -10 penalty for each Rune of Warding on attack Tests or spellcasting Tests targeting you. 

## **Rune of Far Sight**
## **Sls Required** : 10
When the talisman is pressed to the user’s eye, their vision is magnified, allowing them to clearly see events up to a mile away. Two Runes of Farseeing extend vision up to two miles. Three Runes of Farseeing extend vision up to four miles. 

## **Master Rune of Balance**
## **Sls Required** : 20
Whilst wearing this talisman, if an enemy within line of sight casts a spell, you may either Reverse their Spellcasting Test, or Reverse your Opposed Willpower Test (if you’re in range to attempt _Magic Resistance_ ). 

## **Rune of the Furnace**
## **Sls Required** : 10
Whilst wearing this talisman, you can never acquire the _Ablaze_ Condition, are immune to heat exposure, and reduce all incoming Damage from fire and flaming attacks by 4 for each Rune of the Furnace. 

## **Master Rune of Industry**
## **Sls Required** : 20
Whilst wearing this talisman, you may take an extra Endeavour between adventures. 

## **Master Rune of Kingship**
## **Rune of Luck**
## **Sls Required** : 10
Whilst wearing this talisman, you gain 1 Fortune point for each Rune of Luck, which can exceed your usual maximum Fortune. You lose these Fortune points when you remove the talisman (to a minimum of 0 Fortune), and cannot regain them until the following session. 

## **Sls Required** : 24
Whilst wearing this talisman, you may Reverse any Charm, Intimidate, and Leadership Tests you make that target a Dwarf, or a group mostly consisting of Dwarfs. Rumour has it whoever wears this talisman benefits from the wisdom of the previous bearer. 

XI **I** X **VI** XI **I** 

## **Master Rune of Passage Sls Required** : 20
Whilst wearing this talisman, and Moving no faster than walking pace, you can Move through solid, immobile objects like trees, rock, and metal cages. You cannot Move through animals or Undead creatures. You cannot end your Move inside a solid object. 

## **Master Rune of Spite**
## **Sls Required** : 24
Whenever you take Damage from a Melee attack, the attacker immediately suffers 2d10 Damage to a random location, reduced by Toughness Bonus and Armour Points as normal. 

## **Protection Runes**
Protection runes can only be forged upon items of communal significance, such as religious icons, ale kegs, war banners, or permanent installations (sculptures, gatehouses, etc.). Their creation blurs the line between craft and ceremony, and is often undertaken by a priest of the Ancestor Gods. Unlike other runes, which only apply their effects to the bearer, a Protection Rune’s range of effect extends 6 yards, affecting any Dwarf allies within range. Especially well-displayed Protection Runes may extend their benefit further, at the GM’s discretion. 

## **Rune of Discovery**
## **Sls Required** : 8
For each Rune of Discovery the runic item has, the crafter may choose a specific metal or gem (e.g. gold, diamond, gromril, iron ore, obsinite, ithilmar, brightstone). The runic item glows brightly if the specified material appears within its range of effect. 

## **Rune of Enemy Detection**
## **Sls Required** : 8
For each rune, describe a type of creature — a general creature type (Skaven, obvious Chaos worshippers), or a more specific description (one-eyed women with red hair). When a creature that clearly matches the description enters the range of effect, the rune glows a violent crimson. 

## **Rune of Locking**
## **Sls Required** : 6
Any locks within the runic item’s range of effect are immune to being picked or forced except by magic or the corresponding key. Two Runes of Locking also protect from magical effects. Three Runes of Locking are proof against the lock’s corresponding key — only the crafter, or their closest living descendant, can open the lock at will. A lock may still be bypassed by smashing through the chest or door they protect. 

## **Rune of Alarm**
## **Sls Required** : 8
The runic item emits a loud, blaring noise if any creature of Size Small or larger enters its range of effect. Two Runes of Alarm may instead bellow a pre-recorded sentence. Three Runes of Alarm may instead transmit a pre-recorded telepathic message to the crafter or their closest living descendant, over any distance. 

## **Rune of Battle**
## **Sls Required** : 18
Affected allies begin combat with 1 Advantage for each Rune of Battle. 

## **Rune of Purification**
## **Sls Required** : 10
Affected allies gain +20 for each Rune of Purification on Tests to resist toxins in air and water. 

## **Rune of Retribution**
## **Sls Required** : 8
If a creature violates the sanctity of dead bodies within the runic item’s range of effect (e.g. stealing from the dead, casting a necromantic spell), they immediately gain 1 _Ablaze_ Condition for each Rune of Retribution. 

## **Rune of Sanctuary**
## **Rune of Courage**
## **Sls Required** : 14
Affected allies gain +10 on Psychology Tests ( **WFRP Core Rulebook** ) for each Rune of Courage. 

## **Sls Required** : 10
Affected allies gain +10 for each Rune of Sanctuary on Willpower Tests to dispel with _Magic Resistance_ . 

XI **I** X **VI** XI **I** 

## **Engineering Runes**
## **Rune of Slowness**
## **Sls Required** : 12
Engineering runes can only be forged upon Dwarf artillery weapons — specifically Grudge Throwers, Bolt Throwers, or Blackpowder cannons. They are not usually applied to Engineering weapons. 

Enemies attempting to Engage an affected ally reduce the distance they can Run by 4 yards for each Rune of Slowness, to a minimum of the enemy’s Walk distance. 

## **Rune of Accuracy**
## **Rune of Verminkill**
## **Sls Required** : 14
## **Sls Required** : 10
When attacking with this weapon, you gain +10 to hit for each Rune of Accuracy. 

Rodents, Skaven, and rat-based abominations like Rat Ogres lose 2 Wounds for each Rune of Verminkill (ignoring Toughness Bonus and Armour Points) when they enter the runic item’s range of effect, or start their Turn within it. 

## **Rune of Burning**
## **Sls Required** : 16
A target struck by this weapon gains 1 _Ablaze_ Condition per Rune of Burning. 

## **Master Rune of Expel Chaos**
## **Sls Required** : 20
Affected allies may Reverse any Test to resist corrupting influences, Tests to avoid mutation from Corruption, and rolls on the Physical and Mental Corruption Tables. In addition, when an affected ally is engaged with a _Daemonic_ enemy that has the _Unstable_ Trait, they count as having +2 Advantage when calculating Wounds lost for being _Unstable_ . 

## **Master Rune of Grimnir**
## **Sls Required** : 22
You may Reverse enemy Ranged attack Tests made against affected allies. 

## **Master Rune of Grungni**
**SLs Required** : 22 

You may Reverse any enemy spellcasting Tests made against affected allies. 

## **Master Rune of Stromni Redbeard**
## **Sls Required** : 20
Affected allies begin combat with 1 Advantage. Double the range of this rune’s effects to 12 yards, or 24 yards if forged upon a battle standard. 

## **Rune of Forging**
## **Sls Required** : 10
When you Fumble and/or Misfire whilst using this weapon, the crew may activate this rune to negate the effects. You can activate each Rune of Forging once per adventure. 

## **Rune of Penetrating**
## **Sls Required** : 14
The weapon inflicts +2 Damage for each Rune of Penetrating. 

## **Rune of Reloading**
## **Sls Required** : 12
The weapon reduces its _Reload_ Rating by 2 for each Rune of Reloading. If this would reduce the Rating to 0 or below, the weapon loses the _Reload_ Flaw. Weapons with the _Salvo_ Quality cannot be reduced below _Reload_ Rating 1. 

## **Rune of Seeking**
## **Sls Required** : 10
When this weapon attacks a flying enemy, you gain +20 to hit for each Rune of Seeking. 

## **Rune of the Stalwart**
## **Master Rune of Valaya**
## **Sls Required** : 22
Affected allies may Reverse any Willpower Test to Oppose spellcasting with _Magic Resistance_ . The range limit for _Magic Resistance_ is removed — affected allies can Oppose any spell cast against a target in their line of sight — and the Talent can be used to dispel persistent spells ( **WFRP Core Rulebook** ), not just incoming spells. 

## **Sls Required** : 14
Dwarfs crewing this weapon begin combat with 1 Advantage for each Rune of the Stalwart. This extra Advantage is lost by any Characters that leave the weapon’s crew, or become Engaged in melee. 

XI **I** X **VI** XI **I** 

## **Rune of the Valiant**
## **Sls Required** : 10
Dwarfs gain +10 Willpower for each Rune of the Valiant whilst crewing this weapon. 

## **Master Rune of Defence**
## **Rune of Hearth and Home**
The blessing of Valaya affirms a Dwarf ’s resolve to fight and die without fear. All Dwarfs within 25 yards of the Anvil of Doom may count as rolling 01 on any Cool Tests ( **WFRP Core Rulebook** ) they make until the end of the next Round. 

## **Sls Required** : 20
The weapon’s crew always count as being in hard cover, imposing a -30 modifier on Ranged attacks against them. 

## **Master Rune of Disguise**
## **Sls Required** : 20
The weapon is invisible to all enemies until it fires, at which point it becomes visible for the rest of the combat. The weapon’s crew remain visible as normal, and moving the machine still causes noise. 

## **Master Rune of Immolation**
## **Sls Required** : 20
Any Dwarf crewing this weapon may choose to activate the rune as a Free Action, triggering the machine’s self-destruction. All creatures within 6 yards of the machine take 15 Damage to a random location, reduced by Toughness Bonus and Armour Points. Survivors gain the _Ablaze_ Condition. The weapon itself is destroyed. 

## **Master Rune of Skewering**
## **Sls Required** : 22
When making a Ranged attack with the weapon, you may activate this rune to count as rolling 01. If the attack succeeds, it also counts as a Critical, and may strike any location you choose. You may activate this rune once per adventure, and must decide to activate it before you roll. 

## **Doom Runes**
Doom runes can only ever be struck upon an Anvil of Doom (page 97). Crafting a Doom Rune does not require access to a Workshop, nor any materials besides Trade Tools and the Anvil itself. Given how precious an Anvil of Doom is, though, gaining access to use one is a difficult enough task in itself 

Any Character who has learned a Master Rune also learns all three Doom Runes. Instead of an Extended Test, Doom Runes are activated as an Action, requiring a **Hard (–20) Runesmithing** Test. The effects of a Doom Rune can be Dispelled ( **WFRP Core Rulebook** ) as though they were a spell. 

## **Rune of Oath and Steel**
The blessing of Grungni enchants the armour of his children with supernatural resilience. All Dwarfs within 25 yards of the Anvil of Doom improve the AP of any armour they’re wearing by 2, until the end of the next Round. 

## **Rune of Wrath and Ruin**
The blessing of Grimnir unleashes the war god’s fury in a raging storm of splitting earth and darkening skies. All enemies within 25 yards of the Anvil of Doom are struck for 12 Damage to a random location, reduced by Toughness Bonus and Armour Points. 

## **Additional Runes**
the runes in this chapter are but a fraction of those that have been used throughout Dwarf history. some runes are still in regular use, albeit for more niche purposes than those listed here. Other runes were once considered commonplace, but the knowledge to craft them has been lost. Runesmiths seek out and study items that still bear the rune, hoping to reverse-engineer the knowledge to recreate new runic items in their image. 

most fabled of all are the so-called ‘ancestor runes’ — forged millennia ago, rendered inert by the passage of time, but rechargeable when the Winds of magic are at their most tempestuous. When storms of magic roll across the Old World, the boldest Runesmiths retrieve these masterworks and ascend to loci of arcane energy, striking the runes to awaken their godlike power. 

Very occasionally, a sufficiently skilled Runesmith may create a brand new rune. Like all Dwarf institutions, the Runesmith clans view this deviation from ancestral practices with suspicion. All of the great Runelords with master runes named after them had to defy tradition to create their masterworks. 

if a player is interested in learning, discovering, or creating a rune not listed in this chapter, gms should work with them to fulfil their ambitions. The runes in this chapter should serve as a template to write rules for whatever new creations your players can imagine.
